title: Signal Scout — kitchen scraps and rapid proposals (2026-10-29)
content:
Purpose: quick capture of 'kitchen-scrap' signals from customer conversations (support, AE check-ins, onboarding calls) and pragmatic proposals we can trial in 1–2 sprints. Not a polished synthesis — think: sticky notes aggregated into something actionable.

Context: over the last 3 weeks the CS team has been logging short snippets of friction around: model fallbacks, kv-cache mismatches, and token-cost surprises for customers running heavy reranking workloads. These were collected from 9 accounts (mid-market + 3 enterprise pilots).

Topline quick findings (short):
- Customers repeatedly mention opaque cost spikes when switching model variants mid-rollout; perceived as "billing surprise".
- Several customers using Dedicated observed stale KV cache behavior after rollout rotations (cold-start coherence).
- A small group (2 customers) prefer a "preview" mode for responses to catch hallucinations before committing to user-visible logs.
- Embeddings quality drift flagged by one search product after quantized model swap; they want an automatic A/B validation step.
- Docs + error messages around rate-limited streaming were confusing; devs mistook 429 streaming throttles for full request failures.

Representative customer quotes (verbatim snippets captured in calls/slack):
- "We hit a 3x token bill the morning after a variant flip — no heads-up, our pipeline backfilled and cost went nuts." — platform lead, fintech pilot
- "Our reranker returned wildly different top results after the quantized model. It mostly worked but the edge cases got worse." — search eng, retail
- "Streaming errors looked like our call failed entirely. We lost some user sessions because our retry logic tripped." — backend eng, B2B SaaS

Proposed low-friction experiments (ranked by expected cycle time):
1) Billing preflight notice (ETA: 1 sprint; effort: low):
   - Add an opt-in preflight report in Console: estimate expected token rate delta when switching model variants (approximation based on recent 24h usage + model tokenization factor).
   - Quick UX: banner + checkbox when confirming rollout.
   - Why: reduces surprise and gives PMs a control point.
   - Linked quick ticket: INF-3271 (probe lane).

2) KV-cache warmup hook (ETA: 1 sprint spike + follow-up; effort: medium):
   - When a rollout swaps model or instance group, provide an optional warmup route that replays a client-provided prefix set to seed KV caches.
   - Temporary measure: expose an admin-only API to enqueue warmup jobs per-customer.
   - Risk: extra cost for warmups; need controls.

3) Streaming 429 clarification (ETA: < 1 sprint; effort: low):
   - Change streaming SDK docs + error payload to explicitly mark 429-stream frames as throttling warnings, not terminal failures.
   - Add short sample retry logic snippet in each SDK.

4) Reranker A/B validator (ETA: 2–3 sprints; effort: high):
   - Build a lightweight evaluation harness in Optimize that runs a held-out prompt set against current and candidate models, surfaces delta in top-k accuracy and embedding cos-sim differences.
   - Stop-gap: run ad-hoc job for flagged accounts and return a PDF-like diff for CS/Customer.

5) Preview mode for sensitive outputs (ETA: 2 sprints; effort: medium):
   - Console toggle + API flag to ask for a non-committing preview response that can be reviewed and accepted before being persisted/logged.

Quick impact vs effort matrix (text):
- Billing preflight notice: impact = medium, effort = low
- KV warmup hook: impact = high (reduces customer incidents), effort = medium
- Streaming 429 clarification: impact = low-medium, effort = low
- Reranker A/B validator: impact = high, effort = high
- Preview mode: impact = medium, effort = medium

Open questions / unknowns:
- How often do customers flip model variants in automated rollouts vs manual lanes? (we need telemetry)
- Are warmup replays safe for PII-sensitive prompts (customers will want clear guidance)?
- What is acceptable accuracy delta for reranker A/B reports (customer-specific thresholds)?

Immediate next actions (who/when):
- Aisha: raise INF-3271 and attach this note (today).
- Miguel: prototype the streaming SDK snippet and PR for docs (by 2026-11-05).
- Rhea: assemble telemetry query to show frequency of model switches per-customer (by 2026-11-04) and share with eng-sre.
- Samir: scope a 1-sprint spike for KV warmup (est. 3 engineer days) and draft risk controls (by 2026-11-09).

Notes to self / scratchpad bits captured during calls (unpolished):
- possibility: annotate rollout UI with historical token burn line chart for that customer (would help gating).
- small customers want a simple toggle to disable automatic fallbacks to cheaper variants — maybe an account-level policy.
- add customer-visible webhook when warmup completes so they can resume traffic.

Related links / refs (quick):
- Slack thread: #cs-field-scrap — messages 245–268 (2026-10-21..2026-10-27)
- Jira: INF-3271 (billing preflight), INF-3302 (kv-warmup spike)
- Confluence draft: Field Notes — Kitchen Scraps (link above)

Appendix: raw snippets (copied from notes)
- "We only realized when the bill came in — took us three people to trace the blast radius."
- "After the quantized swap our edge-case score fell but p95 latency improved — tradeoff but not acceptable for us."

This doc intentionally short — meant to be shared with product + eng as a starter. Flagging for CS sync on Mon 2026-11-02 to prioritize which of the low-effort experiments to push as tickets.
